migrations.sql:
-- Base operator-auth composes over Orbit's own operators and sessions (the
-- native accounts route). No operator row moves: every operator id, foreign
-- key, access_* row and invitation stays where it is.

-- An operator's authority version is derived from operators.updated_at, which
-- every Orbit change to an operator's email, status or ownership sets. Deriving
-- it adds no trigger or column to operators, so archive schemas are unchanged.

-- How each session issued from now on was proven, beside Orbit's sessions so
-- no existing table changes. Sessions without a row predate Base sign-in and
-- keep their existing 14-day native contract.
CREATE TABLE identity_sessions (
  session_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  kind TEXT CHECK (kind IS NULL OR kind IN ('native','oidc','dev')),
  authority_version INTEGER,
  issuer TEXT,
  subject TEXT,
  sid TEXT,
  provider_id TEXT,
  provider_linked_at INTEGER,
  provider_generation INTEGER,
  proof_at INTEGER,
  proof_version INTEGER
);
CREATE INDEX identity_sessions_provider_idx ON identity_sessions(issuer, subject);

-- One-use email proofs: sign-in links and session-bound step-up challenges.
-- Only keyed digests are stored, never the emailed token.
CREATE TABLE identity_proofs (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
  hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('magic','step_up')),
  operator_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES operators(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  authority_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
  email TEXT NOT NULL,
  session_id TEXT REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  action TEXT,
  return_to TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  used_at INTEGER,
  revoked_at INTEGER,
  CHECK (kind <> 'step_up' OR (session_id IS NOT NULL AND action IS NOT NULL))
);
CREATE INDEX identity_proofs_operator_idx ON identity_proofs(operator_id, kind);

-- Keyed rate buckets for email requests, confirmations and step-up.
CREATE TABLE identity_limits (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, count INTEGER NOT NULL, start INTEGER NOT NULL);

-- The app-owned provider sign-in setting (off for every existing install) and
-- its policy generation: a change ends outstanding provider sessions.
CREATE TABLE identity_settings (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id = 1),
  idp_sign_in INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (idp_sign_in IN (0,1)),
  generation INTEGER NOT NULL,
  first_setup INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (first_setup IN (0,1))
);
INSERT INTO identity_settings (id, idp_sign_in, generation, first_setup) VALUES (1, 0, 1, 0);

-- Provider principals bound to operators; a binding never moves to someone else.
CREATE TABLE identity_bindings (
  issuer TEXT NOT NULL,
  subject TEXT NOT NULL,
  operator_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES operators(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (issuer, subject)
);
CREATE INDEX identity_bindings_operator_idx ON identity_bindings(operator_id);
CREATE TABLE identity_logouts (issuer TEXT NOT NULL, jti TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (issuer, jti));
CREATE TABLE identity_audit (action TEXT NOT NULL, operator_id TEXT, value TEXT, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE identity_guards (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, value INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (value = 1));

-- A delegation credential minted from a local dev session authenticates only
-- behind the checkout's dev key, which a deployed Worker never has.
CREATE TABLE identity_dev_grants (grant_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL REFERENCES delegation_grants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE);

-- Orbit's own magic links are retired: unused links can no longer be redeemed.
-- The empty table stays, so code from the previous release that runs during an
-- upgrade still finds it.
DELETE FROM magic_links;

migrations.name: 0033_identity_providers.sql
migrations.sql:
-- Identity providers (OpenID Connect). Apply as a NEW numbered migration after
-- the accounts schema. Every statement is IF NOT EXISTS, so a store that applied
-- an earlier version of this file applies the current one again as its next
-- migration and gains only what it lacks.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oa_oidc_transactions (
  state_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  binding_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  config_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  payload TEXT NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS oa_oidc_transactions_expiry ON oa_oidc_transactions(expires_at);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oa_oidc_limits (
  bucket TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  count INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
-- One pinned link per configured provider. Linking stores the issuer, JWKS URI,
-- client id, endpoints and allowed algorithms; a changed configuration only
-- records a pending re-link, which the owner completes with a step-up proof.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oa_identity_providers (
  provider_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  preset TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('linked','unlinked')),
  issuer TEXT NOT NULL,
  client_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  jwks_uri TEXT NOT NULL,
  authorization_endpoint TEXT NOT NULL,
  token_endpoint TEXT NOT NULL,
  algorithms TEXT NOT NULL,
  token_auth_method TEXT NOT NULL,
  response_iss INTEGER NOT NULL,
  interface_version TEXT,
  linked_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  pending_issuer TEXT,
  pending_client_id TEXT,
  pending_preset TEXT,
  pending_at INTEGER,
  jwks TEXT,
  jwks_fetched_at INTEGER
);
-- Reachability per configured provider, linked or not. A provider that has
-- failed discovery or JWKS for 5 minutes, or answered 404 or a DNS failure, is
-- hidden from the sign-in page until a later check succeeds.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oa_identity_provider_health (
  provider_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  failing_since INTEGER,
  hard_failure_at INTEGER,
  checked_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

-- OUT-020: whether Orbit adds opt-out headers and a link, per message type. Sequence and
-- workflow email default on. One-to-one email defaults off on a new installation; an
-- installation upgraded with users already present keeps today's opt-out on until an
-- administrator changes it (ct, 19 October 2026), so no consent state changes silently.
CREATE TABLE opt_out_settings (
 message_type TEXT PRIMARY KEY CHECK(message_type IN('one_to_one','sequence','workflow')),
 carries INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(carries IN(0,1)),
 removal_allowed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK(removal_allowed IN(0,1)),
 basis TEXT NOT NULL,
 updated_by TEXT,
 updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
-- Absent rows take the defaults in src/core/features/outreach/opt-out.ts, so a new
-- installation's table starts empty and an archive restores into it.
INSERT INTO opt_out_settings(message_type,carries,basis,updated_at)
 SELECT 'one_to_one',1,'kept on for an upgraded installation',strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ','now')
 WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM operators);
-- A rep's marking on one draft: removal as relationship or transactional mail, or adding opt-out.
CREATE TABLE draft_opt_out (
 draft_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES drafts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
 choice TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(choice IN('relationship','transactional','added')),
 updated_by TEXT NOT NULL,
 updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
-- The opt-out state an approval bound; delivery sends exactly this. Messages approved
-- before OUT-020 have no row and keep the state they were approved with.
CREATE TABLE outbound_message_opt_out (
 message_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES outbound_messages(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
 carries INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(carries IN(0,1)),
 marking TEXT CHECK(marking IN('relationship','transactional','added','transport'))
);

CREATE TABLE outbound_opt_out_capabilities (

);
